classes.name: DeleteWorkPackageDialogComp
classes.description:
# Delete Work Package Dialog Component

This component represents the "Confirm deletion of work package" dialog
that appears when a user chooses "Delete" from a work package row context
menu on the work packages list page.

The dialog contains two buttons:
- Cancel — dismisses the dialog without deleting the work package
- Delete — confirms the deletion and removes the work package

methods.name: clickCancelButton
methods.description: Clicks "Cancel" to dismiss the dialog without deleting.
methods.prerequisites: The delete confirmation dialog is open
methods.observableState: The dialog closes and the work package remains in the table

methods.name: clickConfirmDeleteButton
methods.description: Clicks "Delete" to confirm deletion, then waits for the dialog to detach.
methods.prerequisites: The delete confirmation dialog is open
methods.observableState: The work package is permanently deleted, the dialog closes, and the row disappears from the table

classes.name: NewWorkPackagePage
classes.description:
# New Work Package Page

This class represents the split-view "Create new work package" form rendered
after the user selects a work package type from the toolbar dropdown.

The form is shown on the right side of the work packages page at
`/projects/<id>/work_packages/create_new?type=<typeId>` and contains:
- Subject (required)
- Description (rich text editor)
- People / Estimates / Details sections
- Save and Cancel action buttons at the bottom of the form

After saving, the URL changes to `/projects/<id>/work_packages/details/<id>/overview`
and the application navigates to the work package details page (also rendered
as a split view alongside the work packages table).

methods.name: fillSubject
methods.description:
Fills the Subject field, which is the work package's name and is required
before the form can be saved.
methods.prerequisites: The create work package form is open
methods.observableState: The Subject field contains the given name

methods.name: fillDescription
methods.description:
Fills the Description rich text editor. The editor is a CKEditor instance,
so it is clicked first to ensure it has focus before the text is typed.
methods.prerequisites: The create work package form is open
methods.observableState: The Description editor contains the given text

methods.name: clickSaveButton
methods.description: Clicks "Save" to submit the create form.
methods.prerequisites: The create form is open and the required Subject field is filled
methods.observableState: The work package is created, appears in the table, and the URL changes to `/work_packages/details/<id>/overview`

methods.name: clickCancelButton
methods.description: Clicks "Cancel" to dismiss the create form without saving.
methods.prerequisites: The create work package form is open
methods.observableState: The split-view form closes, no work package is created, and the work packages list is shown

classes.name: WorkPackageDetailsPage
classes.description:
# Work Package Details Page

This class represents the split-view work package details page rendered
after a work package is created or selected. The URL pattern is
`/projects/<projectId>/work_packages/details/<workPackageId>/overview`.

The details panel is displayed on the right side, while the underlying
work packages table remains visible on the left. The page exposes a
"Close details view" button that hides the side panel and returns the
user to the full work packages list view.

methods.name: goBackToWorkPackagesList
methods.description:
Leaves the details view and returns to the work packages table, so the
caller can filter, delete, or assert on rows. Navigates by extracting the
project identifier from the current URL. Throws if the URL does not contain
a project identifier.
methods.prerequisites: The work package details view is open
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to `/projects/<id>/work_packages` and the full table is shown

classes.name: WorkPackagesPage
classes.description:
# Work Packages Page

This class represents the work packages list page in the OpenProject
application, at `/projects/<projectId>/work_packages`.

The page renders an Angular-driven table of work packages, with toolbar
controls for creating, filtering and viewing work packages. Each row
exposes a context menu link that lets the user open the details view,
duplicate, delete, log time, etc.

Notable behaviours:
- The "Create new work package" toolbar button opens a dropdown menu of
  work package types (Task, Milestone, Phase, etc.). The dropdown items
  live in an Angular overlay outside the regular DOM tree.
- The filter panel is hidden by default; clicking "Activate Filter"
  reveals a "Filter by text" textbox that quick-filters the table.
- After saving a new work package the URL changes to the details view
  (`/work_packages/details/<id>/overview`).

methods.name: clickCreateButton
methods.description:
Clicks the "+ Create" toolbar button to open the work package type dropdown.
Use the returned component to select a type (Task, Milestone, Phase, etc.).
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open
methods.observableState: The work package type dropdown opens in an Angular overlay

methods.name: createNewWorkPackageOfType
methods.description:
Opens the create dropdown and selects the requested work package type in a
single call — a convenience wrapper over {@link clickCreateButton} followed
by `selectType`.
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open
methods.observableState: The split-view create form opens for the chosen type

methods.name: clickActivateFilterButton
methods.description:
Clicks the "Activate Filter" button to reveal the filter panel, then waits
for the "Filter by text" textbox to appear. The button toggles, so guard
the call with {@link isFilterActive}.
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open
methods.observableState: The filter panel opens and the "Filter by text" textbox becomes usable

methods.name: isFilterActive
methods.description:
Returns whether the "Filter by text" textbox is visible, which corresponds
to the filter panel being active.
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open

methods.name: fillFilterByText
methods.description:
Clears the "Filter by text" textbox, types the given value, and waits for
the resulting table query to complete before returning.
methods.prerequisites: The filter panel is active — call {@link clickActivateFilterButton} first
methods.observableState: The work packages table re-queries and shows only rows matching the text

methods.name: isWorkPackageVisible
methods.description:
Returns whether a work package with the given subject exists in the table.

The table is paginated (20 rows per page by default), so this method
activates the quick text filter if needed and applies the subject as the
filter value, bringing any matching row into view regardless of how many
work packages exist.
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open
methods.observableState: Side effect — activates the filter panel if inactive and leaves the text filter set to `name`

methods.name: openDeleteDialogForWorkPackage
methods.description:
Opens the row context menu for the work package with the given subject and
clicks "Delete", returning the confirmation dialog so the caller can decide
whether to confirm or cancel. Throws if no matching row is found.
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open and a work package with this subject exists
methods.observableState: The filter is set to `name`, the row context menu opens, and the delete confirmation dialog appears

methods.name: deleteWorkPackageByName
methods.description:
Deletes the work package with the given subject end to end: opens the row
context menu, clicks Delete, and confirms the dialog.
methods.prerequisites: The work packages list page is open and a work package with this subject exists
methods.observableState: The work package is permanently deleted and its row disappears from the table

classes.name: WorkPackageTypeMenuComp
classes.description:
# Work Package Type Menu Component

This component represents the dropdown menu that appears after clicking the
"Create new work package" toolbar button on the work packages list page.

The menu lists the available work package types (e.g. Task, Milestone, Phase,
Summary task) as `menuitem` entries. Selecting a type navigates the user to
the split-view create form (`NewWorkPackagePage`).

The menu items live in an Angular overlay outside the regular DOM tree, so we
scope the root to the `menu` role directly on the page.

methods.name: selectType
methods.description:
Selects a work package type from the dropdown by its visible label. The
label is matched case-insensitively, so "task" matches the "Task" item.
methods.prerequisites: The work package type dropdown is open
methods.observableState: The dropdown closes and the split-view create form opens for the chosen type
